messages:
Incident Bot: PagerDuty alert -> cassiopeia-prod (enterprise tenant) in eu-central showing sustained 5xx spike, incident created.
PagerDuty: Paging Alex (eng-oncall).
Alex (eng-oncall): I'm on it — seeing 5xx from cassiopeia eu-central dedicated pool. Error rate ~17% for the last 3m. latency P95 up to 1.2s.
Alex (eng-oncall): Quick context: cassiopeia is a VPC/dedicated customer with warm standby in us-west (reserved pool). Customer traffic is primarily eu-central though.
Mateo (SRE): Adding myself. Any signs of node failures or autoscaler thrash?
Alex (eng-oncall): Autoscaler stable, nodes healthy. Logs show repeated timeouts connecting to a backing service in eu-central AZ-b (internal). Suspect a downstream dependency causing tail failures.
Priya (Platform): If it's dependency-related, we should failover traffic to warm pool in us-west while we mitigate. TTL on cassiopeia's DNS is currently 300s. We should lower to 30s before switching.
Samir (CSE): Pinged Lina (CSE) to confirm customer impact windows and to prep a message. Lina: customer engineering is online, they report failed requests from EU users. They want a safe stepwise plan.
Lina (Customer Success): Customer aware, asked for no sudden full cutover without canary. They ok with weighted DNS 80/20 then 50/50 if metrics look good.
DNS Admin: I can lower TTL but need engineer to confirm timing. Will schedule TTL change in 30s if someone ACKs.
Alex (eng-oncall): ACK. perform TTL change now.
DNS Admin: TTL set to 30s (propagate pending).
Mateo (SRE): Prep commands for traffic shift. We'll use route-control to set weighted routing on cassiopeia.fleet.redwood.net. Steps: 1) reduce TTL 2) add weight to us-west warm pool 3) monitor 4) expand.
Mateo (SRE): Command I'm about to run (canary 20%):
```
route-control set-weight --tenant cassiopeia --from-region eu-central --to-region us-west --weight 20
```
Alex (eng-oncall): Before you run it, I'll sanity-check health on us-west warm pool.
Alex (eng-oncall): Health check endpoints returning 200 for /health on warm nodes. Sample: `curl -sS https://us-west-warm.cassiopeia.internal/health` -> `\{\"status\":\"ok\",\"kv_latency_ms\":12\}`
Mateo (SRE): Running weighted update now.
Incident Bot: route-control: change submitted by Mateo. Change id: rc-20260315-42.
Mateo (SRE): Change applied: 80% eu-central -> 20% us-west.
Samir (CSE): Starting canary traffic generator at 100 rps to us-west path to validate.
Alex (eng-oncall): Observing metrics: eu-central 5xx from cassiopeia down from 17% to 9% over 90s, us-west healthy at <0.5% errors. Latency for shifted requests ~P95 350ms.
Lina (Customer Success): Customer monitoring dashboard sees decrease in failures for some users. They want another step to 50/50 after 10m if stable.
Priya (Platform): I recommend we also open a routed fallback: keep model-variant fallback in place if us-west experiences capacity issues. Set auto-fallback threshold to 5% errors.
Mateo (SRE): Configured auto-fallback: enabled, threshold 5% (cooldown 60s).
Alex (eng-oncall): While canary runs, engineering will trace the downstream dependency in eu-central AZ-b: logs indicate connection resets from service-x pool. I've opened a ticket with the infra team to investigate.
Mateo (SRE): After 7m canary looks stable. Increasing to 50% per customer request.
Mateo (SRE): Running: `route-control set-weight --tenant cassiopeia --from-region eu-central --to-region us-west --weight 50`
Incident Bot: route-control: change submitted by Mateo. Change id: rc-20260315-43.
Samir (CSE): Notifying customer: "We're shifting 50% of traffic to warm standby while we investigate an internal dependency in eu-central. Expect lower error rates and sub-minute DNS transition."
Lina (Customer Success): Sent message to primary contact and PSA channel. Customer replied: "Thanks, please keep us posted."
Alex (eng-oncall): Metrics post-shift: cassiopeia overall 5xx back down to 2-3%. No capacity alarms in us-west.
Priya (Platform): Recommend we keep weighted routing until root cause is fixed — consider permanent regional routing if dependency fix timeline >4h. Also note cost impact for customer since warm capacity used.
Mateo (SRE): Agreed. For now set a 1hr check-in. Documenting steps in incident tracker.
Alex (eng-oncall): Handoff: I'm leaving for an unrelated page, Mateo take over primary. I'll be reachable but handing to Mateo at 03:25 UTC.
Mateo (SRE): Taking over. Action items for next hour: (1) follow infra ticket on service-x resets, (2) monitor auto-fallback triggers, (3) confirm DNS TTL reverts after stabilization, (4) coordinate any customer-facing updates with Lina.
DNS Admin: TTL 30s will remain until we say otherwise. I can revert to 300s when you give greenlight.
Samir (CSE): Customer asked about access logs for failed requests — I'll gather sample logs and share securely.
Alex (eng-oncall): One more note: we saw one warm node with elevated CPU for a short window; not critical. Monitoring for sustained load.
Mateo (SRE): All right. Marking initial mitigation: traffic successfully shifted to us-west warm pool; canary -> 50% stable; customer notified. Closing immediate page. Will update thread with root cause when infra provides fix.
Incident Bot: Incident status updated -> mitigation in place.
Lina (Customer Success): Thanks team. Customer appreciated the staged approach.
Mateo (SRE): Logging final checks: run `dig +short cassiopeia.fleet.redwood.net` shows mixed A records across regions as expected. Also validating sample traces from shifted requests look clean.
Mateo (SRE): I'll update incident tracker with timeline and handoff notes. If anyone sees regression, re-alert oncall.
Samir (CSE): Uploaded logs to secure bucket and linked in the incident ticket.
Alex (eng-oncall): back on the thread, saw follow-up from infra: transient connection reset from service-x due to config rollback in AZ-b. They are rolling forward fix now.
Mateo (SRE): Good. We'll keep weighted routing until infra confirms fix and eu-central 5xx < 1% for 15m.
DNS Admin: TTL revert scheduled on your signal.
Lina (Customer Success): I'll coordinate a short postmortem note for the customer once root cause confirmed.
Mateo (SRE): Closing operational handoff. Next update in 30m or earlier if anything changes.
Incident Bot: Thread archived after mitigation (metadata: rc-20260315-42, rc-20260315-43).
